title: Sort by a Reference Order
statement:
You get an array items and a reference array order. The values in order are distinct, and every one of them appears in items at least once.

Rearrange items so that values listed in order come first, in the same order they appear in order, with all copies of a value kept together. Values that are not in order go at the end, in ascending order. Return the rearranged array.

examples.why: Both 9s, then both 5s, then the 1. The leftovers 7, 2, 0 are not in the reference, so they go last in ascending order.
Every value is in the reference, so nothing is left over.
Only 6 is ranked. The leftovers keep their duplicates: 4, 4, 8.

constraints: Values in order are distinct and all appear in items
hints: You need a rank for every value: its position in order, or "after all of them" if it is missing.
Sort with a comparator that compares ranks first, and compares the values themselves when both are unranked.
Values are small (0 to 1000), so a counting array avoids sorting: emit order's values by their counts, then sweep 0..1000 for what is left.

explain.intuition:
This is sorting with a custom key. A value's key is its index in order; values missing from order all share a key that is larger than any index, and break ties by their own value. A map from value to index makes each key O(1).

Because values are bounded by 1000, counting is even simpler. Count every value. Walk order and write each value as many times as it was counted, zeroing its count. Then walk 0..1000 and write whatever counts remain; that sweep produces the leftovers already in ascending order.
steps: Count how often each value 0..1000 appears in items.
For each value v in order, append v count[v] times and set count[v] = 0.
pitfalls: Writing each ranked value only once. Duplicates must all be kept.
Leaving the unranked values in their original order instead of ascending.
A comparator that ranks missing values as -1, which puts them first instead of last.

solutions.title: Sort by rank
solutions.idea: Map each value to its position in order; unranked values get a big rank and fall back to comparing values.

solutions.title: Counting
solutions.idea: Count every value, emit the referenced values in order, then sweep the remaining counts from small to large.

followups: Values can now be any 32-bit integer. Which solution still works, and what replaces the counting array?
Leftovers should keep their original relative order instead of being sorted. What changes?
